selected_passages.text:
- Sam Bankman-Fried is currently on trial for seven counts of fraud and conspiracy related to FTX.
- FTX collapsed in November 2022 after exposing a balance sheet showing impossible FTT token holdings.
- Bankman-Fried pleaded not guilty to all charges and faces up to 115 years in prison if convicted.
- Former executives Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty and will serve as key witnesses.
- The trial is represented by Mark Cohen of Cohen & Gresser, who previously defended Ghislaine Maxwell.

selected_passages.text: Bankman-Fried was arrested in December 2022 in the Bahamas, where FTX was based. He was then extradited to the U.S. to face a number of criminal charges. He was released on a $250 million bail bond, and he remained under house arrest at his parents’ home in Palo Alto. This was revoked in August after he was accused of intimidating Alameda’s former CEO, Caroline Ellison, by leaking her private diary.

Bankman-Fried was arrested in December 2022 in the Bahamas, where FTX was based. He was then extradited to the U.S. to face a number of criminal charges. He was released on a $250 million bail bond, and he remained under house arrest at his parents’ home in Palo Alto. This was revoked in August after he was accused of intimidating Alameda’s former CEO, Caroline Ellison, by leaking her private diary.
